meaning.evidence: Every property, limit and table row survives: "T + 1 committee members who get in cahoots can decrypt any ciphertext", "On mainnet, only `Small` (T = 9) can be requested at launch", "Use `getE3Quote` to get the fee". "No single operator can be trusted to mind the inputs" slightly reframes "is acceptable as the custodian" but keeps the point.

sense.evidence: Terms fit: "ticks these boxes", "chip in inputs", "The catch is the computation", "eats into the limited noise budget", "stuff up the result", "stop the E3 dead".

authenticity.evidence: Natural Australian technical English: "stack your task up against a working example", "Kick off with the [CRISP introduction]". Spelling localised: "organisations".

register.evidence: A light-to-middle Aussie touch, closer to level 3 than the level 5 asked: whole lines read plainly, such as "The design can help an application meet data-protection goals." No swearing, though uncle-bob is allowed.

tone.evidence: Keeps the clear, careful developer-doc tone, warnings intact: "The design doesn't, on its own, make an application compliant with a regulation."

flow.evidence: Reads smoothly: "Before you build an auction, make sure your secure process can work out the result within that budget."

variety.evidence: Varied: "ticks these boxes", "chip in", "the catch", "eats into", "in cahoots", "stuff up". "work out" recurs.

essence.evidence: Unmistakably the original page: structure, table, code and link cards kept.

meaning.evidence: The facts survive, including the table and limits: "If T + 1 committee members get together and collude, they can decrypt any ciphertext". One link card loses a point: "Design rules for E3 programs that won't leave you up the creek without a paddle" drops "secure". Asides like "so don't get your hopes up" are colour.

sense.evidence: Most terms fit: "the committee's graft" for work, "Where it comes unstuck is the computation", "chews through the limited noise budget", "a dodgy ciphertext" for malformed, "the whole box and dice". "no skin off anyone's nose if that result is public" strains for "the result can be public".

register.evidence: A full, broad voice through the prose, close to level 5: "Righto, this page runs through the jobs", "The app can hang about for the E3 stages". No swearing, within uncle-bob.

tone.evidence: Keeps the docs helpful, though jokes shade the cautions: "An E3 won't give you a result in real time, so don't get your hopes up."

flow.evidence: Reads well, with a few padded lines: "The whole private voting app, start to finish, from circuits to client."

variety.evidence: Wide range: "chip in", "hang about", "whips up", "legit", "comes unstuck", "chews through", "graft", "leg up", "Knock up".
